body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-08 while validating the Spanish completion in #1469.

The checked-in `messages.pot` lists **2397** unique msgids. The source tree actually
yields ~**2595**. The 198-string gap is not noise: each one was checked and found
verbatim in `cps/` (e.g. "A duplicate scan is already running…" in a template,
"Callback domain is not verified…" in `cps/gdrive.py`, "LDAP Server not reachable"
and "Kobo sync for Magic Shelves is disabled globally…" in `cps/web.py`,
"Cleared sync state for book…" and the title-sort rule message in `cps/admin.py`).

Why it matters: translators sync their catalogue from the pot. Every locale except
`es` sits at exactly **2373** unique msgids — ru, de and fr all measure identically,
which is the signature of a shared stale source rather than a coincidence. Those
translators cannot translate the 198 strings because the strings are not in the file
they are handed. No amount of translation effort can close the gap; de/fr/it can
never reach 100% until the pot is regenerated.

`es` is at 2645/2645 only because @HaruIjima-kun extracted fresh rather than working
from the checked-in pot. That is the workaround, not the fix, and it is invisible to
anyone who follows the documented process.

Fix: regenerate `messages.pot` from source (SPA msgids must stay anchored in
`cps/spa_strings.py` or auto-translation strips them) and run `pybabel update` across
locales so the new msgids appear as untranslated rather than absent. Verify after with
`msgfmt --statistics` per locale — the untranslated counts should RISE, which is the
correct outcome: the work becomes visible instead of hidden.

Measured on merged main (72e718f30):
    es 2645 translated
    pl 2609 translated, 36 untranslated
    ru 2622 translated, 23 untranslated
    de 1891 translated, 124 fuzzy, 630 untranslated
title: messages.pot is stale, so ~198 real user-facing strings are invisible to every translator
